title: [Performance] Optimize Qwen PLE prefill with Triton on Ascend
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it

Optimize Qwen PLE prefill on Ascend with a prefill-only Triton module. The Ascend model binding selects the path once: prefill calls `ple_conv_prefill`; decode and speculative decoding call upstream `ple_conv`. There is no single-request special case or backend-selection environment variable.

The prefill path materializes the four-tap weights as contiguous `[tap, channel]` data, reads channels contiguously, skips history-state loads when a tap comes from the current chunk, and uses a measured 2048-channel tile with eight warps. The separate state-writeback kernel preserves old history until every token has read it. Multi-request batches, token remapping, initial history, null state slots, and both state strides are supported. This replaces the earlier PyTorch prefill implementation in this PR.

The model-local binding remains under maintainer review. The required Ascend Qwen model adaptation is present in main; this PR supersedes #20269.

### Validation

- In `qjj_flash_main` on Ascend 950DT with vLLM `544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542`, an isolated checkout of the final PR source passed all four NPU nightly operator tests. The tests verify exact output and final state against upstream, and explicitly verify mode routing through the model binding. Actual import paths were checked before testing.
- Earlier diagnostic kernel sweeps covered 62 BF16/FP16 cases, including mode semantics, token maps, both state strides, optional residuals, 4096/8192-token inputs, and channel tails. The final PR module is prefill-only; decode/spec use upstream directly. Final module cleanup was revalidated by the nightly suite.
- Focused final-dispatcher full-call timing at BF16 and 8192 total tokens: 0.876 ms for one request with channel-stride-12 test state, and 0.758 ms for four requests with channel-stride-one state (the current vLLM default layout). These are isolated operator times, not service TTFT.
- Focused Ruff lint/format, Python compilation, and diff checks passed.

### Follow-up

- Model ownership and patch removal are tracked in #20384; rewire the PLE operator after that refactor is integrated.
- Validate service-level TTFT and broader hardware/configuration coverage.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542
